title: How do you line up eight big numbers from smallest to greatest?
description: Farhan sorts eight raffle tickets at a school fair. The video groups the numbers by the ten thousands place and then compares thousands and hundreds.
teaching_notes: One idea: compare from the left, one place at a time, and move to the next place only when the places before it match. Watch for hundreds being compared before thousands.

source: Let Us Do 3, arrange in increasing order
video_script.why: The child can compare two numbers but has not yet ordered a whole list of five digit numbers.
video_script.substitution: Group the numbers by the ten thousands digit, then compare thousands, then hundreds inside each group.
video_script.anchor: Farhan sorting numbered raffle tickets at a school fair
video_script.wrong_answer: forty thousand, four hundred and seventy-three is greater than forty-seven thousand, three hundred and forty
video_script.wrong_move: Chintu says forty thousand, four hundred and seventy-three is greater than forty-seven thousand, three hundred and forty because four hundred is more than three hundred. He skipped the thousands, and forty-seven thousand is more than forty thousand.
video_script.payoff_line: the eight tickets are now in order from smallest to greatest

final_answer.spoken: eighteen thousand nine hundred and twenty-six, thirty-four thousand four hundred and seven, thirty-four thousand seven hundred and forty, forty thousand three hundred and forty-seven, forty thousand four hundred and seventy-three, forty-seven thousand three hundred and forty, seventy-three thousand four hundred and four and seventy-four thousand four hundred and thirty

maths_rules: 34,407 vs 34,740: thousands 4 and 4 are equal; hundreds 4 < 7, so 34,407 < 34,740
40,347, 40,473, 47,340: thousands 0, 0, 7; so 47,340 is the greatest of the three; hundreds 3 < 4, so 40,347 < 40,473
video_script.design: Exercise: order eight five digit numbers. Hint: look at the ten thousands digit first. The row of eight tickets stays on the stage and the sorted row is built below it.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='fair'/>Farhan sells raffle tickets at a school fair. He lays out eight tickets on the table.
<bookmark mark='a'/>Two tickets read forty thousand, three hundred and forty-seven, and thirty-four thousand, four hundred and seven.
<bookmark mark='b'/>Two more read forty thousand, four hundred and seventy-three, and thirty-four thousand, seven hundred and forty.
<bookmark mark='c'/>Two more read seventy-three thousand, four hundred and four, and seventy-four thousand, four hundred and thirty.
<bookmark mark='d'/>The last two read forty-seven thousand, three hundred and forty, and eighteen thousand, nine hundred and twenty-six.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Put the tickets in increasing order, smallest first.

narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='chintu'/>Forty thousand, four hundred and seventy-three is greater than forty-seven thousand, three hundred and forty. Four hundred is more than three hundred.
<bookmark mark='hund'/>He looked only at the hundreds.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>The thousands come first. Forty-seven thousand is more than forty thousand, so he skipped the place that decides.

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Group the tickets by the ten thousands digit. Only one ticket has one in that place, so it goes first.
<bookmark mark='three'/>Two tickets have three there. The thousands match, so look at the hundreds. Four hundred is less than seven hundred.
<bookmark mark='place'/>Thirty-four thousand, four hundred and seven comes before thirty-four thousand, seven hundred and forty.

narration: <bookmark mark='four'/>Three tickets have four in the ten thousands place. Their thousands are zero, zero and seven.
<bookmark mark='last'/>Forty-seven thousand, three hundred and forty is the greatest of the three. The other two differ in the hundreds, and three hundred is less than four hundred.
<bookmark mark='seven'/>The last two have seven in front. Three thousand is less than four thousand, so seventy-three thousand comes first.
<bookmark mark='pay'/>The eight tickets are now in order from smallest to greatest.

narration: <bookmark mark='cmp'/>To check, compare each ticket with the one next to it, from the left.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>Stop at the first place where the two numbers differ. The bigger digit there wins.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Does each ticket in your row come before a greater one?
